newsitem.title: PERU: Southern Peru's 5-month output rises 1.58 percent.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru's 5-month output rises 1.58 percent.

text.p: Copper mine output at Southern Peru Ltd reached 125,303 tonnes in the first five months of the year, up 1.58 percent compared with the same period last year, the government said Friday.

Majority owned by ASARCO Inc and Peru's largest copper producer, Southern accounted for 61 percent of Peru's total output of 205,017 tonnes in the first five months, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
These figures were for copper produced at Southern's Cuajone and Toquepala open-pit mines.

Five-month output at the country's second largest producer, Magma Copper Co's Tintaya mine, rose 26.48 percent to 28,814 tonnes. The former state-run Tintaya mine was sold to U.S.-based Magma in November 1994.

Output in the same period from Cyprus's Amax Minerals Co's Cerro Verde open pit, Peru's third largest copper producer, rose 34.77 percent to 22,018 tonnes. Cerro Verde was privatized in December 1993.
At state-run Centromin Peru, the fourth largest producer, production dipped 2.26 percent to 15,436 tonnes.
Copper is Peru's largest single export earner, accounting for about one-fifth of total Peruvian exports.
